newsitem.title: CHINA: China boosts state natural gas prices 9-32 pct.
newsitem.headline: China boosts state natural gas prices 9-32 pct.

text.p: China has raised prices of natural gas under the state plan by a range of nine to 32 percent, the official China Chemical Industry News said on Thursday.

The move brought the well-head price set by the state for fertiliser production to 480 yuan ($57.80) per 1,000 cubic metres from 440 yuan, for a nine percent rise, the smallest of the current round of increases.

Prices paid for natural gas for residential use will climb 26 percent to 580 yuan per 1,000 cubic metres from 460 yuan while natural gas for other uses will be increased 32 percent to 690 yuan per 1,000 cubic meters from 520 yuan.
A new category of commercial use natural gas covering restaurants, shops and the entertainment industry was created with a price set at 830 yuan per 1,000 cubic metres.
The price increases excluded natural gas from major producer Sichuan province in the southwest and the Tuha field in the far western region of Xinjiang.
The new prices were approved by the State Council and the State Planning Commission. The report did not comment on the increases and did not specify when the price changes would take effect.
It said that natural gas outside the state plan was unaffected by the move. Delivery terms were also unchanged, it said.
